title: An Empirical Study on Using Large Language Models to Analyze Software Supply Chain Security Failures
review_status: full-text audit complete; source corpus, manual-agreement baseline, per-label accuracy, mitigation ratings, prompt tuning, and validity boundaries checked
sections_checked: manual label construction and inter-rater agreement
evidence_note: For 69 reports, GPT accuracy is 59% compromise type, 88% intent, 74% nature, 52% impacts; Bard is 28%, 88%, 69%, 45%. Manual impact-label agreement is low (κ=0.34). Advice mean rating is 3.83/5 and depends on report detail. Prompts were tuned on newest 20%; Bard shared the GPT-tuned prompts and had a 2,000-token limit. Authors position LLMs as analyst aids, not replacements.

title: Lessons from the Long Tail: Analysing Unsafe Dependency Updates across Software Ecosystems
review_status: full-text audit complete; npm sample, six regex features, tier prevalence, merge rates, and non-confirmation of maliciousness checked
sections_checked: npm library/PR population and tier construction
evidence_note: From 63,829 update-related PRs in 1,500 purposively selected npm libraries, six regex features flag 12,465 PRs across 1,027 libraries. At least one flagged PR appears in 81% top, 80% middle, and 44% bottom libraries; merge rates are 70%, 71%, 79%. Authors state the feature heuristic does not confirm maliciousness; actual exploitability remains open.

title: "I see models being a whole other thing": An Empirical Study of Pre-Trained Model Naming Conventions and A Tool for Enhancing Naming Consistency
review_status: full-text audit complete; user survey, repository corpus, DARA evaluation, metric inconsistencies, and generalization threats checked
venue_year_verified: arXiv v3 revised 2025-08-18; published EMSE 2025; frozen frame period follows 2023 first submission
evidence_note: Mixed-method study of 108 Hugging Face users and 14,296 popular PTM names. DARA body/table reports 99% model_type accuracy but abstract reports 94%; architecture accuracy is 72%, and task top-1 accuracy is 72.3% in Table 14 versus approximately 76.3% in narrative. Task top-1 F1 is 56.5%. Evaluation is shuffled 5-fold on a 4,108-package dataset; authors note imbalance, exclusions, and registry scope. Exact v3 study data run through 2024. Metadata mismatch detection is not provenance or security validation.

title: Towards Measuring Supply Chain Attacks on Package Managers for Interpreted Languages
review_status: prior full-text audit reconciled for exact frozen sample version; not counted as a new read
venue_year_verified: exact arXiv v2 audited in batch 7; 2021 publication record
evidence_note: MALOSS reports 339 new suspicious/malicious packages and maintainers confirmed/removed 278. This is not an unbiased prevalence estimate; static accuracy and dynamic coverage are limited, scope is narrow, and the pipeline can be evaded.

title: Routing with Privacy for Drone Package Delivery Systems
review_status: prior full-text audit reconciled for exact frozen sample version; not counted as a new read
sections_checked: four Boston geography scenarios and limitations
venue_year_verified: exact arXiv v2 audited in batch 30; ICRAT 2022 paper
evidence_note: Defines route-conditioned vendor-customer inference risk and compares heuristics to enumerated Pareto fronts for six orders. Geography can allow simultaneous privacy/efficiency improvement or force a tradeoff. Boston scenarios assume 20m/s, one minute per stop, fixed orders, passive route-only observer; no field privacy outcomes.
